title: Batteries are now cheaper than natural gas turbines used at many data centers
key_facts: A new Wood Mackenzie report finds four-hour batteries cheaper than open-cycle gas turbines in all 43 markets it surveyed, on every continent.
Open-cycle gas turbines are a type of gas plant favoured by many data centre developers and often used as peaking plants.

Data centre developers buying every turbine they can get have pushed up gas turbine prices; open-cycle turbines now take two to four years to procure and closed-cycle waitlists extend into the early 2030s.
Wood Mackenzie predicts battery electricity costs will keep falling while gas turbine costs rise over coming decades.
Solar is the cheapest new power in every market surveyed, though North American solar prices are 'under pressure' from tariffs and import restrictions.
In the Middle East and Africa four-hour batteries will be 33% cheaper by 2035; in China storage costs are 55% below its neighbours'.
Wood Mackenzie principal analyst Ahmed Jameel Abdullah: 'This economic shift is decisive and widening.'
quote_evidence: Battery storage is now cheaper than a type of natural gas power plant favored by many data center developers, according to a new report from Wood Mackenzie.
On every continent and in each of the 43 markets that Wood Mackenzie surveyed, four-hour duration batteries were less expensive than open-cycle gas turbines.
why_it_matters_hint: Cheaper batteries could ease power costs as data centres drive demand.
notes: Consultancy's own report as relayed by TechCrunch; the report itself was not opened.
